sources.title: A bunch of Grand Theft Auto games will be cheap on Steam until GTA 6 comes out, and only one sucks
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's November 19 launch, Rockstar has multiple classic Grand Theft Auto games on sale on Steam – and, nearest I can tell, only on Steam. The Nintendo Switch eShop actually has a competing deal for the Grand Theft Auto Definitive Edition Trilogy, which is down 67% to $19.79, but that sale ends in 11 hours from the time of writing. On Steam, several GTA games are discounted until November 19 for an obviously timed special promotion. On Steam, you'll find four games on sale via two actual products: You can't argue with GTA 4 for $6, but you might argue with this version of, in particular, GTA 3. The Definitive Edition Trilogy was famously panned at launch for wonky graphics and poor technical performance that, for the most part, has been patched up in the years since. However, the PC port for GTA 3's Definitive Edition is uniquely poorly rated for reasons that will sound familiar. Here's how the three games in this trilogy compare in Steam reviews: The reception to the two other games in the trilogy improved over time while GTA 3 steadily declined. Much like the day-one reviews, today's Steam players complain of Rockstar launcher interference, bugs, shoddy art, broken cinematics, and performance dips. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Curiously, perhaps unrelated to the quality of the port, some of today's gamers also don't seem to take too kindly to GTA 3's design sensibilities, it being slightly older than Vice City and San Andreas, and certainly a rawer open-world experience. Thomas Williamson, the CEO of the outsourced trilogy's original developer, Grove Street Games, said earlier this year that the criticism faced at launch was deserved. "I agreed with most of the people's reactions," he said. "But unfortunately, I feel like we did not agree with how the game was released and the response to it from a development side. And I think that would have changed the narrative significantly." However, he added, "at the end of the day, looking at the behind-the-scenes metrics on those games, there were a lot of people who were playing them and really enjoying them." You won't find Grove Street Games listed on the store pages for these games anymore. Previously, Williamson called it a "dick move" for Rockstar to have Grove Street's name removed. GTA 6 being pirated is just "a fact of life," says CEO of Rockstar owner, and lawyers are ready if it becomes a problem Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Rockstar's having a sale on old GTA games on the only platform Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't coming to (ours)
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives on November 19, but not for us, no—the big day is only for gamers on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. We're not being completely excluded, though: We can't have GTA 6 in November, but we can take advantage of pre-release discounts on a bunch of older GTA games—deals that, ironically, don't appear to be available on consoles. As noted by GamesRadar , there are four GTA games available in two releases: Grand Theft Auto 3, Vice City, and San Andreas bundled up in the GTA Trilogy for $19.79/£19.79/€19.79—67% off the regular price—and Grand Theft Auto 4: Complete Edition , which includes The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony expansions, for $6/£5.09/€6, a 70% discount. Those aren't the deepest discounts ever seen, but Grand Theft Auto games typically don't venture into the 90% off territory we all enjoy so much—and according to Isthereanydeal.com, this is as low as the GTA Trilogy has ever gone, and close to the mark for GTA 4 . You may recall that the GTA Trilogy Definitive Edition was a mess when it launched in 2021, but it seems to have turned that frown upside-down since then: On Steam, where the trilogy arrived in 2023, Vice City and San Andreas both hold "very positive" ratings. GTA 3 is stuck at a "mixed" rating, which is unfortunate: Glancing at user reviews, it sounds like the game still isn't in perfect shape, but it's also suffering from the fact that it's 25 years old, and was the first 3D game in the series—some jank and roughness was there right from the start. Grand Theft Auto 4: The Complete Edition, on the other hand, doesn't suffer from those shortcomings. It's getting pretty long in the tooth too—it came out in 2008—but represents a shift in design and tone that led the series into what it is today. If you're looking for just one older GTA game to horse around with, this is the one, especially given that it's less than half the cost of the trilogy. As mentioned, these sale prices are currently only being offered on Steam: There's currently no sign of any of them on either the Xbox or PlayStation stores (Fun fact: there actually is no digital version of GTA 4 on the PS Store because Sony didn't start selling full-priced games online until well after 2008). Maybe it's just coincidence, but they do appear to be intentional pre-GTA 6 sales: The discounts are on until November 19, when Grand Theft Auto 6 launches—except on PC. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have 55 Trophies/Achievements
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to be a completionist’s dream. It has been racking up more side content promises than any game to come in the series thus far; there are indications it’s the longest single-player campaign in franchise history, and the world is absolutely gargantuan. That means we can expect a substantial array of GTA 6 Trophies and Achievements to surface, depending on your platform of choice. In fact, thanks to a recent comment on social media, we know how many are coming, and it’s more than Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 had at launch. Rockstar Games is all about the ultimate immersion in Grand Theft Auto 6. As they said in a recent interview, they want you to live a life inside GTA 6, which is set to drop in just 11 days, on November 19th. It’s likely the densest Grand Theft Auto title ever made . While you’re immersed, you’ll be able to chase a thick assortment of Trophies and Achievements. The former if you’re on PlayStation, and the latter if you’re an XBOX player, of course. What’s interesting is that Grand Theft Auto 6, with 55 Trophies/Achievements , beats both Grand Theft Auto 5 (51) and Red Dead Redemption 2 (52). It’s not a huge edge, but it’s an edge nonetheless. It’s also worth pointing out that GTA 5 eventually went on to get 78 Trophies/Achievements with the addition of GTA Online content over the years, so there’s every opportunity for GTA 6 to do the same thing. Hell, perhaps this will be the first Grand Theft Auto 6 title to get a single-player expansion since GTA 4. If you want to go the whole hog and 100% Grand Theft Auto 6, you’ll be pleased to know that data suggests there are both a Platinum Trophy and a Mythic Achievement. The latter is the new tier that XBOX put in place in recognition of players who have gone the distance with their games. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches November 19th on XBOX Series X|S and PlayStation 5, and pre-loading will start globally on November 10th. Are you looking forward to GTA 6? sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Square Enix accidentally botches a Nier: Automata update, balloons required file size from 50GB to 366GB on PC
sources.text: "Do you think games are silly little things?" Yesterday, Nier: Automata received a new patch on Steam, adding more language support to the title - it can now be played with Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese options - but this new update also, somehow, inflated the file size of the game on PC from about 50GB to 366GB. D'oh! What's worse is, the update is not optional. The cause of this, reportedly, is a bug that caused all the DLC in the YoRHa Edition of the game to become the same size as the base game - and the new download stacks them all concurrently. "Only SquareEnix can turn 40GB into 366GB with 8GB patch," says one dissatisfied Steam reviewer. If you don't have space for this massive new file on your PC (and I can't say I blame you, it's ridiculous), there is a workaround, as confirmed by Square Enix in a tweet via its Japanese Twitter account . "We have confirmed an issue where, following the latest update to the Steam version of Nier: Automata, the installation process indicates that more storage space is required than expected," noted the publisher. "We are currently investigating the cause and working on a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game by unchecking the DLC under Steam → Properties → DLC." It's quite ironic, really, that so many Steam reviewers are complaining about things like "I just need to delete 90% of my computer to install this" when a large part of the game is managing the software/programmes installed on your android protagonists in order to upgrade your abilities and stats. There's even an ending for uninstalling your OS on your mechanical main characters. I'd be inclined to suggest this is some sort of meta psy-op from creator Yoko Taro , but… nah, that's just fantasy, isn't it? Isn't it? Speaking of Taro, earlier this year we learned that " Nier Automata will continue ", though we only heard back in 2025 tha t most of the projects the developer was working on were cancelled . One of these may have been the Tencent -backed Nier mobile game in 2024, which reportedly "struggled to find a monetisation to offset its high costs ."

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Nier: Automata developer is 'currently investigating' a bizarre update bug that drastically inflated the game's file size from 50GB to 366GB
sources.text: Square Enix is 'working to resolve the issue'. Usually, it's a good thing when a patch makes an already excellent game substantially larger. But in the case of Nier: Automata 's most recent update, bigger is most certainly not better. On Friday, the beloved action RPG from Square Enix received what should have been a straightforward update to add localisation support for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Korean languages. But as reported by Automaton Media, the update also increased the game's file size from 50 gigabytes to a staggering 366 (and a half) gigabytes. "We have identified an issue following the latest update for Nier: Automata … where installation requires significantly more storage space than intended," wrote Square Enix in a Steam post . "We are currently investigating the cause and working to resolve the issue. We apologise for the inconvenience." It isn't clear how this issue has occurred, but it may be related to Nier: Automata's DLC. When selected for download on Steam, each DLC appears to have the same file size as the base game. Weirdly though, this is only true for the initial download and installation. Once the game is installed, the file reportedly reverts to a more appropriate size of roughly 50 gigs. Indeed, as a temporary solution, Square Enix suggests that anyone who needs to download Nier: Automata deselects all eight DLC when they do so. "As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game using the intended amount of storage space by going to "Properties" à "DLC" in Steam and unchecking each DLC item." While 366 gigabytes is obviously a ridiculous size for a game, what's frightening to me is that games are on track to become that massive in the coming years. Big budget games regularly exceed the 100 gigabytes in file size these days, while several major titles like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, have surpassed 200GB. One of the largest reported installations to date is for the combat simulator DCS World , which had a maximum file size of 250GB back in 2021 . So although Nier: Automata's SSD-choking file-size is an accidental anomaly, it might also be an ominous glimpse into the future of PC gaming. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. stories.title: How to trade all the Masks from the Happy Mask Shop in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: How to trade all the Masks from the Happy Mask Shop in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: The Skull Mask, the Spooky Mask, the Bunny Hood, and more are part of the Happy Mask Shop quest in OOT Remake The Happy Mask Shop in Zelda Ocarina of Time has you run around Hyrule trading masks with characters for Rupees, including the Skull Mask, Spooky Mask, Bunny Hood, and the Keaton mask. Though these masks only serve as commodities to be traded with specific characters, if you can allocate all four to the right characters and complete this OOT quest, the Happy Mask Shop will give you access to four new masks that all have a very specific utility. Below I'll show you how to hand out all the Masks and the specific locations you need to look. Keep in mind that the Switch 2 version is the same as the original, in that the Happy Mask Shop won't open in The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time until you open the passage to the Goron City. Fortunately, the guard who opens the passage will actually tell you that the Mask Shop is now open, flagging that you can start this questline. Bought from the Mask Shop for 10 Rupees, you need to give this to the Guard in Kakariko Village who opens the passage for you, the same one who lets you know that the Mask Shop is open. He'll give you 15 Rupees in return. Bought for 20 Rupees, head back to the starting area of Kokiri Village, where you start off and get the first Shield and Sword in Zelda Ocarina of Time , and turn North into the Lost Woods. The moment you enter, head left through the hollow trunk to meet The Skull Kid, playing a tune on top of a log. He, understandably, will offer to take the Skull Mask from you, though only pay you ten for it. Cheapskate. After buying the Spooky Mask for 30 Rupees, head back to Kakariko Village, and this time take the East exit to the Graveyard, but do so during daytime. Here you'll find a boy wandering around. Speak to him to give him the Spooky Mask, for which he'll give you 30 Rupees back. The final mask in this sequence is bought for 50 Rupees. You can only sell it once you've progressed to the point where you have obtained the Three Spiritual Stones in the main story. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week Once this happens, head to Hyrule Field. There'll be a man who runs in circles around the field, practicing his running. If you go during the night, he'll be sitting beside the road and you won't have to keep pace. Either way, if you give him the Bunny Hood, he will entirely fill your wallet with Rupees, so it's a good idea to have expanded it as much as possible prior to the trade to really capitalize on that. Having given these masks out, the Happy Mask Shop will now have four new masks in store that you can get, all of which serve a particular function. Here's what they do: It's really only the Mask of Truth that provides the major advantage to gameplay, though some of the dialogue options and reactions from NPCs can prompt interesting lore information. Likewise, the cash infusion delivered by the Bunny Hood NPC can make Link incredibly rich, a great reward in and of itself. © GamesRadar+. Not to be reproduced without permission. sources.title: Zelda OOT Remake: All Kakariko Village Cucco locations
sources.text: All Kakariko Village Cucco locations in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake The Cucco Lady has lost her Cuccos, and itâs up to Link to get them back in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Timeâs new remake. Cuccos are basically the chickens of Hyrule, and the Cucco Lady is allergic to them. An awful allergy to have considering what her name and job are. The Cuccos have escaped and are exploring Kakariko Village at their leisure. In this guide, weâre breaking down how to return them to the Cucco Lady and the rewards youâll get for it in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time âs Nintendo Switch 2 remake. All of the Cuccos are located outdoors, and within Kakariko Village â no need to head up Death Mountain Trail or into the Graveyard. When you find a Cucco, pick it up and carry it over to the Cucco Ladyâs pen. Throw the Cucco inside to bank it. If you need to throw or put down a Cucco outside of the pen, donât worry, it wonât move too far away from where you place it. Just donât attack them. There are seven Cuccos to find in total. The first Cucco is located near the entrance to Kakariko Village. It really is as simple as that. The second Cucco can be found near the Cucco Pen; itâs inside the building site. Near the building site is a pile of bricks, and a Cucco is sitting on top. When holding a Cucco above your head, you will glide through the air when jumping. While holding one of the Cuccos youâve already found, jump from the ledge up the stairs next to the Cucco Lady. Youâll be able to reach the bricks from there. Throw both Cuccos down before getting down from the bricks. Thereâs a single wooden crate near the house on the lowest level of the village, next to the path leading up toward the Death Mountain Trail gate. Break this crate by rolling into it to reveal a Cucco hidden inside. Grab a Cucco to glide with and carry it up to the windmill entrance. You can jump off the left side of the platform while holding a Cucco to clear the fence. Just beyond the fence, youâll find a Cucco on the ground. Climb the stairs and throw both the Cucco you carried over and the one on the floor here over toward the well, where you can take them back to the pen â but donât jump back over yet. From the point beyond the fence described in the fifth Cucco location, climb the ladder that leads up the hill and behind the windmill. Thereâs another Cucco up here that you can use to glide back down to safety and collect the Cuccos youâve used. The final Cucco you need is located near the buildings leading toward the Death Mountain Trail. Very easy to find. Once youâve finally collected all seven Cuccos and put them back in the pen, the Cucco Lady will reward you with an Empty Bottle. If you havenât played Ocarina of Time before, this might seem like a meagre reward, but trust us, itâs incredibly valuable, and youâll be happy to have it.

sources.title: Zelda OOT Remake: All Masks and where to sell them
sources.text: All Happy Mask Shop masks and who will buy them in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s remake One of the trickiest side objectives in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the Switch 2 remake is the Happy Mask Salesman quest. After you open the Death Mountain Trail path in Kakariko Village, youâll be able to start renting and selling masks from a new shop in Castle Town Market. Thereâs a man outside the shop thatâll hint at who might want to buy the masks you sell, but his hints are vague and donât give the details youâll need. In this guide, weâre breaking down every mask in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Who buys them, how much they cost, and all the masks you can rent after quest completion. Each mask has one potential buyer and can only be sold once. You can rent the same mask repeatedly, but youâll only be able to sell each of the initial four once each. The Death Mountain Trail guard is the one you show Zeldaâs Letter to, and heâll ask you to go to the Happy Mask Shop after â this is the signal that the quest is now available, and the guard will be your very first customer. The first Skull Kid you meet in Kokiri Forestâs Lost Woods will buy the Skull Mask. We have detailed directions for navigating the Lost Woods , but the quick instructions are as follows: enter the Lost Woods, immediately turn left, and youâll find the Skull Kid standing atop a tree stump. Stand on the stump opposite while wearing the Skull Mask and talk to him to initiate the sale. He only has 10 Rupees, so youâll need to make up the difference. The small boy that plays in Kakariko Graveyard by day will happily buy the Spooky Mask so he can better imitate DampÃ© the Gravekeeper and his Grave Digging Tour . The boy is only around during the day, but will happily buy the Spooky Mask at cost. The Running Man will only appear on Hyrule Field after completing the third dungeon, Lord Jabu-Jabuâs Belly. When returning to Hyrule Field from Zora Domain, youâll likely see the Running Man jogging across the field. Talk to him while wearing the Bunny Hood, and heâll pay a whopping 200 Rupees for it before sprinting across the field far faster than ever before. Once you return to the Happy Mask Shop after selling all four masks, youâll be given access to the special reserve masks to rent. These masks cannot be sold; theyâre merely for cosmetic purposes. All except for one, that is. While wearing the Mask of Truth, youâll be able to hear the thoughts of the person youâre talking to before the conversation starts. In addition, youâll now be able to communicate with the Gossip Stones dotted around Hyrule â these are the mysterious stones with the Sheikah Eye symbol on them. Each Gossip Stone will share a hint or sometimes even some lore.

sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake reportedly running at 60 fps on PC just hours after game's official Nintendo Switch 2 release
sources.text: Visual and performance issues not quite ironed out yet, which will be music to Nintendo's ears. I've spent all night playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2, and it's a fantastic experience, but some would prefer to tinker and toil over an emulator than enjoy Link's new look. The game is already running on PC, but performance issues are aplenty. You can see progress is moving pretty fast from the emulator crowd, just from these two videos by Unreal Gaming PC on YouTube. Published on the game's official launch day, November 5, this video shows the game getting over the splash screen and running the cutscenes fairly well; however, it suffers from bad flickering, stuttering, and frame rates around the 20-30 fps mark during gameplay. 12 hours later, another video. This time showing the game running between 30–60 fps during gameplay, albeit with some persistent flickering and stutters throughout. There's undoubtedly still a long way to go to a playable experience to match the native Switch 2, but that's marked progress for half a day's work. Especially considering the game is designed for an Arm-powered handheld with very different hardware to what's running the emulator ( Ryzen 7 9800X3D , 64 GB of RAM, and RTX 4080). User akakevinvro on X also posted a video claiming a pretty steady 60 fps. Both are running on the Lichii emulator for the Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. It's called the "VERY experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator" on its GitHub page. It's an open-source project that has similarities to projects of the same ilk, such as Yuzu. Yuzu's developers settled a legal dispute with Nintendo of America and shut down development of the emulator in 2024 . Nintendo has a long history of taking down projects it deems to infringe on its rights, while emulators such as the now defunct suyu often argue that they do not circumvent Nintendo's privacy measures. sources.title: Nintendo exec says "new games and remakes both have a place" following Zelda: Ocarina of Time launch
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is finally out in the wild a good 28 years after Nintendo's original gem dropped back in 1998, and is already proving to be the highest-rated game of 2026 thus far. Sure, it's a remake, but it slots in nicely between all the other new games – and it's still just as valuable, too, as Nintendo senior vice president of product development and publishing Nate Bihldorff explains to Polygon . "I do think that new games and remakes both have a place in the Nintendo stable, of equal importance to be honest. There are fans of every single IP that we have out there," as he says. Remakes are very welcome to those fans, to say the least. "Of course, having new games in those series is wonderful, and I look forward to them as much as anyone else does, but there's also a deep satisfaction in revisiting games that were very, very special, like Ocarina of Time" – and that's evident in how well the remake is doing already, if you ask me. It made Metacritic's top 30 games of all time within a day, proving that the community is very much happy to enjoy remakes as it is entirely fresh titles. Longtime Legend of Zelda fans aren't the only people immersing themselves in Nintendo's revamped spin on Hyrule, either. As Bihldorff states, "It's also important to think about how many people had never played the original, and for them, the remake of Ocarina of Time is going to be an absolutely brand-new, 2026 experience, and one that I just cannot wait for them to get their hands on." A quick look at social media proves his assertion here right. Remakes don't just cater to old fans, but they help introduce countless more to long-standing franchises and series like The Legend of Zelda. They certainly don't take away from new releases, either – every fellow Zelda stan I know is on the edge of their seat waiting for more announcements from Nintendo, especially after the likes of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom . I don't see that changing, ever. While you're here, be sure to read our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review. You can also check out our Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock live blog if you want to grab one of Nintendo's highly-sought-after new consoles. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week After spending years with her head in various fantastical realms' clouds, Anna studied English Literature and then Medieval History at the University of Edinburgh, going on to specialize in narrative design and video game journalism as a writer. She has written for various publications since her postgraduate studies, including Dexerto, Fanbyte, GameSpot, IGN, PCGamesN, and more. When she's not frantically trying to form words into coherent sentences, she's probably daydreaming about becoming a fairy druid and befriending every animal or she's spending a thousand (more) hours traversing the Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3. If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand. sources.text: Goron City and Darunia in the OOT Remake have players try to cheer up the gloomy Goron Goron City in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake is a fiery mountain home, run by the equally fiery Darunia, who is miserable for a number of reasons and will need cheering up if you want his assistance. To do so will require a bit of a runaround, taking you all the way to the Lost Woods and back again, but it's worth it (and also mandatory if you want to progress the plot of the Switch 2 Remake). If you're having trouble working out what to do next, I'll explain how to solve the mystery of Goron City in a full walkthrough and guide, taking you through all the steps needed in this section of The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time. If you're approaching Goron City, you'll need to be prepared against fire. Find out how to get a metal, non-flammable shield in our guide on how to get a Shield and Sword in Zelda Ocarina of Time . When you first reach Goron City in the Ocarina of Time Remake, you'll discover that all the Gorons are miserable and that their leader, Darunia, has holed himself up in his room. The main goal here is to access Darunia and cheer him up . Here's how you do that: With Darunia placated, he'll be willing to give you Spiritual Stone of Fire... Except he doesn't have it. You'll have to go to the Dodongo Cavern and find it there. Fortunately, he will give you Goron Bracelet, which will allow you to pick up Bomb Flowers and throw them! Feel like some side quests? sources.title: This Is One Of My Favorite Stupid Details They Kept In The Ocarina Of Time Remake
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is full of the usual intended goofiness the series has always had, but sometimes it was moments of unintentional goofiness that really elevated the original Nintendo 64 game. With the remake out on Switch 2 now, it would have been easy for Nintendo to scrub some of that stuff out, but as some players have found, some of the funnier opportunities for player-driven silliness are still included in the game, including the fact that the Iron Boots can ruin serious cutscenes. The Iron Boots are a piece of equipment Link can wear to walk under the surface of water, allowing him to reach places he wouldnât be able to swim to. Theyâre often paired with the Zora Tunic, which allows Link to breathe indefinitely, and these two items together are crucial for places like the Water Temple which has Link going in and out of fully submerged areas. However, because these Iron Boots weigh Link down, they also let out clanking sounds as he tries to walk with them. Still, the game lets you put them on anywhere you want, and if you don them when Link has to walk across an area for a serious moment, youâre gonna hear him coming. As players are discovering, this quirk is still in the remake, and somehow, the boots are even louder coming through the Switch 2âs speakers. [OoTHD] Oh boy.. shouldn't have equipped. by u/JeszicaJeanette in zelda Though fans are discovering the remake has sanded away some of the originalâs rough edges , and taken out some exploits that fans have taken advantage of for nearly 30 years, itâs nice to see that not everything has been completely polished this time around. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. Could a remake of the other (better) Nintendo 64 Zelda also be on the way? sources.name: PlayStation Blog
sources.title: Hozy brings calm, tactile home restoration to PS5 on November 9
sources.text: Are you ready to meet your new cozy favourite? Imagine actually enjoying cleaning your house or ripping out old tiles. Unhinged, isn’t it? You put on your favourite music and open the windows to let the fresh air in. The dust disappears, the floor begins to shine with every sweep of the mop, and the rooms start to transform into cozy, welcoming spaces. There’s something incredibly satisfying about seeing it all come together, one step at a time. That’s exactly what we wanted to capture in Hozy – a cozy, tactile and stress-free home restoration game that is coming to PlayStation 5 on November 9. Hozy is a game where you can completely unwind. There are no timers, no scores and no pressure. Each level in Hozy features a space with its own atmosphere and story. Your first job is to tidy it up and renovate it. Then furnish it using the sets of furniture and décor provided. Don’t worry about being overwhelmed with an endless catalogue – each level features a carefully curated set of items you’ll need so that the end result always looks worthy of the interior design magazine. To help you tackle the tasks of refurbishing the rooms with ease, you’ll have access to an array of tools: from a simple mop to a crowbar. We all know what it’s like to mop the floors… But in Hozy, even this is a real pleasure. We’ve done our best to ensure that using each tool brings nothing but joy. You can also interact with the surroundings and a whole host of furniture. Open the window to let the breeze play with the dust particles. Light a lamp by the sofa to create a cosy reading nook. Play a tune on the piano or find secret messages in one of the drawers – experiment with different objects to discover what other interesting effects await you. Every surface, every object and instrument has its own unique sound. And the music changes dynamically as you progress through the level – we recommend playing with headphones or a home cinema system to fully appreciate the sounds of the world around you. This is something we’re particularly proud of. When we first started developing Hozy, our main aim was to make using the instruments as enjoyable and responsive as possible. And the DualSense wireless controller is simply perfect for complementing and enhancing that experience. Thanks to haptic feedback, interacting with objects and surfaces becomes even more realistic, as every action you take is accompanied by a unique set of vibrations. For example, when a mop glides smoothly across the floor or when you’re arranging furniture. Combined with the adaptive triggers, you’ll naturally feel the resistance of the floorboards as they finally give way to the crowbar. The DualSense’s built-in speaker helps you immerse yourself even further in the game’s atmosphere, subtly emitting additional sounds from the instruments you are currently using. Once you’ve completed the Hozy storyline, comprising nine unique levels, your journey into the world of cosiness isn’t over yet. Come back to the houses you’ve already restored to discover… new versions of the previous rooms. The ‘Game+’ mode will help you look at these rooms in a new light (literally) – now you can switch between day and night, as well as furnish rooms with different sets of furniture. Some of them will change beyond recognition. If you fancy creating something truly yours, Hozy has just the thing for you – a Sandbox mode with every item available in the game. Mix and match, duplicate, and customize your rooms however you wish. Who are we to tell you which wallpaper, background colour, window shape, support beams or light switches to choose? But there’s more: we also have plans for seasonal events and various DLCs, both free and paid. Of course, we haven’t forgotten about the various accessibility features, so that as many renovators as possible can enjoy Hozy. The game is available in 11 different languages and includes a range of visual and control settings. Adjust the movement speed of your tools, invert the camera, change colour display settings and much more. If you want to make playing Hozy even more comfortable – settle into your favourite armchair, pour yourself a cup of hot chocolate and launch the game on PlayStation Portal. We’re looking forward to November 9, when you’ll be able to enjoy Hozy at your own pace.

sources.title: Hozy for PS5, Xbox Series launches November 9
sources.text: Cozy renovation and cleaning game Hozy will launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 9, publisher tinyBuild and developer Come On Games announced . Hozy first launched for PC via Steam on March 30. A Switch version is also planned for release in 2026. Here is an overview of the game and “Hideaways,” via tinyBuild: Wrap yourself in a cozy atmosphere where every small action and detail matters. Hozy is about slowing down. There are no timers, scores, penalties, and absolutely no stress or pressure. Just you, your tools, and the simple joy of making spaces beautiful again. Whether you’re wiping windows, repainting walls, or finding the perfect spot for a sofa, everything is designed to keep you in a calm, satisfying flow. Skip the endless catalogue overwhelm. Hozy offers a carefully curated selection of furniture and decor for each level that work well together. Place items freely, rotate and arrange them however you like—there is no right or wrong and no room is ever the same. Use the tools at your disposal wisely, and you’ll create spaces worthy of an interior-design magazine!

sources.text: MARVEL Cosmic Invasion ’s Castle Doom mode gets extended gameplay ahead of its November 10 DLC launch, with branching paths and 12 perks. The DLC launches simultaneously on PC via Steam, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, PlayStation 4 and 5, and XBOX Series X|S. This is the second DLC for MARVEL Cosmic Invasion. The first launched on May 18, bringing X-Men’s Cyclops and Fantastic Four’s The Thing to the roster of the Beat ‘Em Up title. At launch, the roster included Wolverine, Spider-Man, Venom, Captain America, and Iron Man. The game initially launched in December 2025 and has since accumulated over 2 million players. In addition to the new game mode mentioned above, this next DLC pack will include new characters. The playable characters are Doctor Doom and The Invisible Woman.
